subject: Re: Post-demo: model fit recommendations + quantization tradeoffs
messages:
From: Amir Qureshi <amir@solara.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Thanks — quick recap + constraints

Olga / Ben,

Really appreciate the demo today — it clarified a lot. Quick recap from our side and a couple of constraints so you have full context: 

- Goal: Replace our current endpoint for customer-facing extraction and summarization with something that is both cheaper per-token and stays within 150ms p95 for single-turn API calls.
- Input profile: average prompt length ~120 tokens, expected output ~220 tokens, 80% of calls are single-turn (no long KV cache use).
- Quality bar: must match or exceed our existing rouge-like scoring on our evaluation suite (we shared sample prompts) — false positives in extraction must be <5% on core entity set.
- Ops: we'd like a recommended migration path (model + quant profile) that shows expected latency & cost delta vs current.

Attaching the public prompt set and the CSV we used for baseline numbers. Next steps: if you can share a short list of recommended models and quant profiles + a few benchmark numbers, we can line up an internal PoC (engineering + procurement) next week.

Thanks,
Amir
Head of ML Ops | Solara Analytics
(attachment: solara-prompt-sets-v1.xlsx, solara-benchmark-raw.csv)

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Amir Qureshi <amir@solara.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Thanks — quick recap + constraints

Amir — thanks for the clear recap and for the prompt/benchmark files. Short read of what we ran and our recommendation for an initial migration path: 

1) Candidate models (ranked by expected quality -> cost tradeoff):
   - LlamaX-13B-Orig (FP16 baseline): highest match to your extraction set; p95 will be ~170-200ms depending on instance type.
   - LlamaX-7B-FT (AWQ 4-bit recommended): very close on precision for extraction tasks, ~20-30% lower cost vs 13B with minor regressions on tail cases.
   - Mosaic-Lite-6.9B (GPTQ tuned): best cost/latency but some edge-case entity misses we saw in 3% of samples.

2) Quantization/throughput playbooks we suggest to evaluate in PoC:
   - AWQ 4-bit (preferred start): maintains decoder fidelity for extraction prompts; expect ~1.6-2.0x throughput improvement vs FP16 with minimal quality delta on your prompt set.
   - GPTQ 4-bit (profiled): cheaper footprint and slightly faster, but showed small precision drops on nested entity extraction; recommend as a later step if AWQ doesn't meet cost targets.
   - FP8 / mixed-precision (experimental): promising latency but larger variance across instance types; use only if latency SLO is tight and you can tolerate extra regression testing.

3) Preliminary bench highlights (short):
   - On our rtx-a10g equivalent, LlamaX-13B FP16: p95 ~185ms, token cost baseline.
   - LlamaX-7B with AWQ4: p95 ~120ms, cost ~45% lower per request, precision drop ~1.8% absolute on your extraction set.
   - Mosaic-Lite-6.9B GPTQ4: p95 ~95ms, cost ~60% lower, precision drop ~3.2% absolute.

4) Suggested PoC plan (2-week cadence):
   - Week 0: sandbox endpoints + share minimal eval harness (we will run your prompt set + holdout).
   - Week 1: run AWQ4 on 7B and FP16 on 13B, collect latency/cost/quality.
   - Week 2: run GPTQ variants and iterate prompts/temperature settings; decide target model & rolling plan.

I've uploaded the raw benchmark CSV and a short runbook at: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/solara/2026-11-28

Next step: Ben — can you schedule a short technical sync with Solara engs early next week? Amir — if that sounds good, we'll provision PoC capacity and share a cost estimate.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Amir / Olga — putting some concrete numbers and ask list below so procurement/eng can action quickly: 

Bench detail (attached CSV contains per-sample rows):
- Baseline (your CSV): current vendor avg latency 210ms p95, cost baseline X.
- Redwood ran three runs against your prompt set:
  * LlamaX-13B FP16: p95 185ms, pass rate 96.2% on core entity set.
  * LlamaX-7B AWQ4: p95 120ms, pass rate 94.4% (absolute -1.8%).
  * Mosaic-Lite-6.9B GPTQ4: p95 95ms, pass rate 93.0% (absolute -3.2%).

Procurement asks / decision points for PoC: 
1) Which latency/cost target is primary? (e.g., p95 <=150ms vs cost <= -50%)
2) Can we run PoC on a small committed instance for 2 weeks (we'll discount trial costs if you commit to procurement timeline)?
3) Any regulatory constraints on hosting or data persistence (encryption at rest, retention periods)?

Bench attachments: solara-benchmark-raw.csv (per-sample), solara-prompt-sets-v1.xlsx (prompts + expected outputs).

If the priority is p95 <=150ms with <=2% absolute quality delta, our recommendation: LlamaX-7B + AWQ4 as the first migration candidate. If Solara wants more aggressive cost/latency, Mosaic-Lite + GPTQ is the lane but we'd pair it with a targeted prompt augmentation to recover edge-case misses.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
(attachment: solara-benchmark-raw.csv)
